correctness.rationale: The boundedness proof uses cubic exterior drift and finite directional-height integrals, avoiding the nonproper-Lyapunov trap; positivity and exact dissipation follow by differentiating H. Summable O(n^-3/2) radius and O(n^-3/2) return-time errors yield the finite phase-corrected limit. All real µ and nonzero initial conditions are covered; exact polynomial symbolic checks run from the included artifact.

value.rationale: The zero-linear-damping boundary is the natural weak-focus threshold of the exact model studied by Gasull–Giacomini. The quantitative original-time return-rate and renormalized phase classify the global observable spiral: a universal energy envelope but a parameter-dependent, sign-independent long-term frequency chirp. The existence of a finite corrected phase for arbitrary initial conditions is structurally useful for phase matching and comparing critical oscillatory transients; it is not an arbitrary parameter slice or a known-table recomputation.
